title: MUSA evaluation report (tools/run_task.py --output)
description: Guide §4.7/§4.8. run_task.py emits two report shapes from one entry point: `static` (audit, case-override and golden checks, no device) and `full` (every case evaluated). The mode decides which stage blocks are present, so it is validated by value the same way the task tier is. The report is a derived artifact produced by a tool this schema does not own, so the properties are permissive: the invariants pinned here are the mode, the tier, and the fact that `summary.passed_overall` is always present and always agrees with `summary.exit_code`.

runtime.description: The submission's own work at steady state, in milliseconds, taken the way the framework takes it and a baseline is measured: a MUSA event pair around each call, the L2 cache flushed before each one, the first timed call discarded, and the mean of what is left. Not the process's wall clock -- that is `wall_ms`, and it is dominated by the device's first-call initialisation and by mapping a library the size of muDNN.

stability.description: Guide §4.7's stability re-run: whether the case agreed with itself when it was run again with the same seed and the same inputs.

max_abs_error.description: The worst absolute difference between the produced tensors and the golden, before the tolerance decides.

model_state.description: What the compiled path staged beyond the case's own tensors. The reference's state is a function of the case's seed, its parameters and the framework's construction order, so a torch-free submission cannot rebuild it: the evaluator materializes it for that case, stages it beside the case's inputs and records here whether it did, what it produced and which configuration it built from. `digest` covers the whole state, so a drift (a different torch, a changed construction) is a named mismatch rather than a wrong number.

case_id.description: The case the state was built for. Its parameters, not the problem file's defaults, decide the construction.

init_inputs.description: The reference's `get_init_inputs()` for this case, as the state was built. Two cases of one task can differ here (a case re-binds module constants), which is why the state is per case.

wall_ms.description: The whole process's wall clock for this case, in milliseconds, for a reader who wants the real cost rather than the steady-state one.

timing.description: The measurement the runner reported. Null means the runner printed no per-call times, in which case `runtime` fell back to the process wall clock.

warmup.description: Calls made to bring the process and the device to a steady state before any timed call.

repeat.description: How many timed calls the submission was measured over; `samples` holds them.

discarded.description: Timed calls thrown away before the recorded ones, as the framework discards its first trial.

timer.description: What took the time: `musa_event` is a MUSA event pair around the call, as the framework uses, and `host_clock` is an older runner.

cache.description: `cold` when the runner flushed the L2 cache before every timed call, as the framework does; `warm` when it could not allocate the buffer.

l2_thrash_bytes.description: How many bytes the runner wrote to evict the cache before each timed call; zero means it did not.

mean_ms.description: The mean of `samples`, in the format `kernelbench.timing.get_timing_stats` uses.

samples.description: Every timed call, so a reader can re-derive the number the row carries.

mode.description: static: the audit and the golden cross-check without a device. full: the Python-module path end to end. binary: the compiled path end to end, where the submission runs in its own process and imports no torch.

build.description: Guide §4.7. The build stage: whether the submission compiled, and the compiler output when it did not. §5's step 8 puts it after the audit so a rejected submission never spends a compile, and before the link check because that check reads what the build produced.

libraries_linked.description: The contract's whitelist, resolved onto libraries that exist and passed to the build script.

whitelist_entries_without_a_library.description: Whitelist entries that name no library the machine has. They are not errors: the contract may name an operation (SDPA) rather than a file, and a task whose answer never links it should not fail for that.

environment.description: Present when a device stage could not reach the stack it needs. An environment failure is not a submission verdict, so it is reported as its own block with its own exit code rather than as a failed case.

link_whitelist.description: Guide §4.7's B-tier-only stage: which libraries the build products actually link, read off their dynamic sections. `checked` counts the artifacts whose dynamic section could be read; an artifact that could not be read is an error rather than a skip, because "could not read it" and "links nothing" are different facts.

after_evaluation.description: A second read of the same directory once the cases have run, reported separately because a submission may compile lazily on its first forward call, which leaves the up-front stage with nothing to read.

submission_artifact.description: The executable the build produced, named so a report can be reproduced from it.
